name: Mars
fact: Earth–Mars launch windows open every 26 months — driven by orbital resonance. Miss the window and wait two years.
bio: The highest eccentricity of the inner planets (e=0.093) — Mars swings ~20% farther from the Sun at aphelion than at perihelion, driving big seasonal and dust-storm swings. Launch windows, by contrast, are set by the ~26-month Earth–Mars synodic period.

science_sections.why: Mars's 25.2° axial tilt is remarkably close to Earth's — but combined with its eccentricity, southern summers are intensely hot and short while northern summers are long and mild.
Mars's 0.0935 eccentricity (six times Earth's) gives a 20 % swing in solar flux per orbit — the engine behind global dust storms that can engulf the planet for months.
Mars launch windows open every 26 months — the synodic period between Mars and Earth — and Hohmann transfer is why every Mars mission departs in one of those windows.
Mars has two small captured-looking moons — Phobos (orbiting below synchronous altitude, spiraling inward) and Deimos (slowly receding).
Mars hosts the densest active spacecraft census beyond Earth — orbiters from five agencies and surface rovers / landers from three.
